question: at 90% on CICIoT2023 after two epochs, does the pruned students' lower calibration error survive when the dense reference and every student are each given their own temperature fitted on held-out validation rows
motivation: notebooks 40 and 46: the dense reference's confidence exceeds its accuracy by 0.22 (shallow) and 0.27 (deep) after two epochs; students better calibrated in 71 of 80 paired cells. Temperature scaling (Guo et al., 2017) is the standard post-hoc fix and a reviewer's first objection

design.models: dense teacher and the committed notebook 40 90% structures for magnitude, Taylor, Fisher; both networks
design.recovery: two full epochs, notebook 46's recovery and recalibration code unchanged; seeds 601, 701, 809 (notebook 46's two-epoch seeds)
design.temperature_fit: one scalar T > 0 per recovered and recalibrated model, minimising the mean negative log-likelihood of softmax(logits / T) over log T in [log 0.05, log 20] (bounded scalar minimisation), on a fit set of validation rows disjoint from the evaluation subsample and the natural-prior sample: at most 2,000 rows per class, seed 7
design.evaluation: notebook 46's class-balanced evaluation subsample (primary) and 200,000-row natural-prior sample; 15-bin equal-mass ECE and mean confidence minus accuracy, before and after scaling

readings.C_raw: per network and rule: paired ECE (student minus dense) before scaling, 95% paired t interval; counts better / worse / straddling
readings.C_scaled: the same after each model's own temperature
readings.T: fitted temperatures, dense and students, mean and range over seeds
readings.overall: advantage_is_temperature if after scaling at most two of the six cells keep the student interval below zero and none has it above zero; advantage_survives if at least four of six keep it below zero; students_worse_after_scaling if at least two of six have it above zero; mixed otherwise

expectation.T1: after scaling the dense reference's ECE is at most 0.05 on both networks and the reading is advantage_is_temperature

reporting_rule: every reading reported as measured; whichever way it reads, Section IV-D of the paper states it
